title: Initial-horn filtration of a simplex product
statement: Use simplicial sets, simplices, horns and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define $\partial\Delta^m$ as the union of all proper faces of $\Delta^m$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. For integers $m\geq0$ and $n\geq2$, there is a finite sequence of simplicial subsets $X_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_t=\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$, starting with $X_0=(\partial\Delta^m\times\Delta^n)\cup(\Delta^m\times\Lambda_0^n)$. For every $1\leq s\leq t$, there are integers $q_s\geq2$ and $0\leq p_s<q_s$ and a map $\sigma_s:\Delta^{q_s}\to X_s$ whose restriction to $\Lambda_{p_s}^{q_s}$ factors through $X_{s-1}$, and the resulting square with rows $\Lambda_{p_s}^{q_s}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{q_s}$ and $X_{s-1}\hookrightarrow X_s$ is a pushout (the colimit of this span). If $p_s=0$, the composite $\Delta^{q_s}\to X_s\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$ sends vertices $0,1$ to $(0,0),(0,1)$ respectively.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 4.4.4.7 (01DN), assertions (1) and (2), including the endpoint condition. Read statement and complete free-simplex proof online 2026-10-17. This is a Kerodon tag, not the unrelated Stacks tag. Archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], a $q$-simplex of the product is a weakly increasing sequence of $q+1$ pairs in $[m]\times[n]$. It is degenerate exactly when two consecutive pairs coincide: then the sequence factors through the surjection identifying those positions; conversely a degeneracy repeats a pair. Thus nondegenerate simplices are strict chains. Call such a simplex free if both coordinate projections are surjective and its chain contains $(p,0)$ and $(p,1)$ for some $p$. Since every first coordinate below $p$ must occur before $(p,1)$ and the second coordinates there are zero, its initial chain is exactly $(0,0)<\cdots<(p,0)<(p,1)$. Consequently the two displayed vertices occupy positions $p,p+1$, and no other vertical $0$-to-$1$ pair occurs; call $p$ its index. In a strict chain the sum of the two coordinates increases at least once at each step, so its dimension is at most $m+n$. The finite poset $[m]\times[n]$ therefore has finitely many strict chains. Enumerate its free simplices as $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_t$, first in increasing dimension, and within each dimension in decreasing index, resolving remaining ties arbitrarily. Let $X_s$ be the subset generated by $X_0$ and the images of the first $s$ free simplices. Faces and degeneracies of these images remain in those images, so $X_s=X_0\cup\bigcup_{a\leq s}\operatorname{im}(\sigma_a)$ is already a simplicial subset. This defines a finite increasing sequence.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, definition of free simplices and ordered enumeration (lines 60-72 of the online text).

proof.text: Consider a strict chain $\tau$ outside $X_0$. Its first coordinates contain every element of $[m]$, and its second coordinates contain every $1,\ldots,n$: otherwise the corresponding projection lies in a proper face or in the zeroth horn, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $(p,1)$ be its first vertex of second coordinate $1$. Every first coordinate $a<p$ must occur earlier, since it cannot occur after $(p,1)$; its second coordinate is zero there. Thus the chain before $(p,1)$ is $(0,0)<\cdots<(p-1,0)$, possibly followed by $(p,0)$. If $(p,0)$ occurs, $\tau$ is free. If it does not, insert $(p,0)$ immediately before $(p,1)$; both projections of the resulting strict chain are surjective, and it is free with index $p$. Hence $\tau$ is the $p$th face of a listed free simplex. Every weak chain is obtained from its strict chain of distinct pairs by repeating entries, so this also accounts for every degenerate simplex. It follows that $X_t=\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, claim that the ordered free simplices exhaust the product (lines 77-91).

proof.text: Fix a free simplex $\sigma=\sigma_s$ of dimension $q$ and index $p$, with initial chain $(0,0)<\cdots<(p,0)<(p,1)$. For each face deleting position $a\ne p$, verify membership in $X_{s-1}$. If $a<p$, its first projection omits $a$, so the face belongs to $X_0$. If $a=p+1$, a next vertex exists because the second projection contains $2$ (here $n\geq2$). If its second coordinate is at least $2$, deleting $(p,1)$ omits $1$, so the face belongs to $X_0$. Otherwise that next vertex is $(p+1,1)$: it has first coordinate greater than $p$ by strictness and cannot skip $p+1$ by surjectivity. Insert $(p+1,0)$ in the face just before $(p+1,1)$; the resulting free $q$-simplex has index $p+1$ and is earlier in the enumeration, so contains the face. If $a>p+1$, deletion either loses a required coordinate and gives a face in $X_0$, or preserves both surjections and the vertical pair, giving a free $(q-1)$-simplex, again earlier. This puts every face other than the $p$th in $X_{s-1}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, the three face cases preceding the missing-face argument.

proof.text: The missing $p$th face $\tau$ retains all first coordinates and all second coordinates $1,\ldots,n$, hence is outside $X_0$. Its initial chain is $(0,0)<\cdots<(p-1,0)<(p,1)$ and it has no vertical $0$-to-$1$ pair. If it belonged to $X_{s-1}$ it would be a face of an earlier free simplex $\sigma'$. It is nonfree of dimension $q-1$, whereas earlier simplices have dimension at most $q$; thus $\sigma'$ is obtained by inserting exactly one vertex into $\tau$. Apply [lem-cbc-nonfree-chain-completions]: inserting $(p,0)$ recovers $\sigma_s$, and the only distinct possibility has index $p-1$ and exists only for $p>0$. That possibility occurs later, since equal dimensions are ordered by decreasing index. This contradiction excludes the missing face, also when $p=0$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the only strict subchains of $[q]$ outside $\Lambda_p^q$ are $[q]\setminus\{p\}$ and $[q]$ itself: every other proper subchain omits some vertex different from $p$. Containment of the full simplex would imply containment of its missing face. Together with step 3 this proves $\sigma_s^{-1}(X_{s-1})=\Lambda_p^q$ on strict chains, and hence on weak chains by collapsing repetitions.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7 proof, final missing-face contradiction and inverse-image equality.

proof.text: The strict vertex chain of $\sigma_s$ is injective, so postcomposition with it is injective on the weak chains in every degree. Thus $\Delta^{q_s}$ is isomorphic to its image, $X_s=X_{s-1}\cup\operatorname{im}(\sigma_s)$, and their intersection is the image of $\Lambda_{p_s}^{q_s}$ by step 4. Given simplicial maps $g:X_{s-1}\to T$ and $h:\Delta^{q_s}\to T$ agreeing on this horn, define the map on $X_s$ by $g$ on the first subset and by $h\sigma_s^{-1}$ on the image. It is well-defined on the intersection, commutes with every simplicial operator because the two subsets are closed under those operators, and is the unique extension since they cover $X_s$. This is exactly the pushout universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], using the natural-transformation definition in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Each free simplex surjects onto the $n+1$ vertices of $\Delta^n$, so $q_s\geq n\geq2$; its vertical pair occupies positions $p_s,p_s+1$, hence $0\leq p_s<q_s$. If $p_s=0$, those first two vertices are precisely $(0,0),(0,1)$ by step 1. This proves all remaining clauses.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.7, final pushout verification; elementary direct gluing argument for the embedded strict-chain simplices, replacing the appeal to the more general Lemma 3.1.2.11.
